title: Name the reader
summary: Tell the tool who will read the result. This helps set the words and amount of explanation. Still check that the facts remain correct.
introduction: Tell the tool who will read the result. This helps set the words and amount of explanation. Still check that the facts remain correct. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Tell the tool who will read the result. This helps set the words and amount of explanation. Still check that the facts remain correct.

blocks.code:
Task: explain a loop in programming.
Reader: a class 5 learner who has never coded.
Style: short sentences and one school-day example.
blocks.title: Name the reader

blocks.text: The reader description asks for beginner language. The school example can connect repetition to something familiar, such as ringing a bell each day.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add an instruction to explain any new word.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Simple language should not introduce a false explanation.
For more detail later, use this [Prompt Engineering further reading](https://www.promptingguide.ai/introduction).
